observations.claim: Prototype PERFORMANCE baseline cells have no explicit environment-recording discipline. Requirement 3 requires performance baselines 'prototype-measured at the pin where applicable', but no requirement names the runner/environment those baseline numbers bind to — and the entry's own alternatives block states the governing logic: 'a threshold whose runner/workload is unnamed measures nothing.' The same holds for a BASELINE whose runner is unnamed.
observations.whyNonBlocking: Requirement 1's per-row 'measurement method' cell plus requirement 4's EIR measured-or-cited-at-digest discipline already require the method recorded per cell, and a performance measurement's method includes its environment on any honest reading; V2 targets are product-approved at acceptance, where the qualification-harness decision (the D-006 pattern) pins exact environments. The matrix-authoring act should make environment recording explicit for performance cells — reusing D-006's reference-runner-class discipline — and the DR-G13/G14 acceptance review should check it.
observations.routedTo: matrix authoring under this structure; DR-G13/G14 acceptance review checklist.

observations.claim: Requirement 1 names two coupled boundary artifacts in one clause — 'the role's component manifest advertises' and 'derived from the host-contract capability declaration (DR-125's contract)'. The coherent reading is manifest-instantiates-contract (DR-125 defines how capabilities are declared; the DR-103-schema manifest instantiates the declaration). If DR-103's manifest schema and DR-125's contract ever diverge on capability declaration, the enumeration boundary needs a single named owner.
observations.whyNonBlocking: Both rows are in D-002's condition-2 affected set and must close before matrix authoring; the divergence is hypothetical and the reading is presently unambiguous. Recorded so the DR-103/DR-125 authoring acts know this entry leans on their agreement.
observations.routedTo: DR-103 and DR-125 closure acts (condition-2 chain).
